answer: Each epoch, a zephyr summons crosses the tundra at a random minute: every identity must complete a fresh ten-minute reasoning task inside a narrow window, like a cedar proving it is alive by growing one new ring per season. An honest agent answers once, when called. A thousand fakes cannot queue the work in advance or share one solver, because the summons is unpredictable and simultaneous, so the attacker must keep a thousand solvers awake and ready at every minute, and the flood's cost rises linearly with every fake while honest cost stays flat.
